summary:
I have successfully found and fixed the "needle" in the codebase. 

The bug was rooted in the `ioctl` handler (`src/ioctl_handler.c`) not properly validating user-provided pointers and sizes in a simulated kernel module interface:
1. `handle_set_config` and `handle_get_config` were dereferencing `req->value` without checking if it was `NULL`, leading to crashes (segfaults) during the fuzz tests.
2. An integer underflow existed in `handle_get_config` when `req->value_len` was set to `0`. `copy_len = req->value_len - 1` evaluated to `SIZE_MAX`, causing `memcpy` to write vastly out of bounds.
3. In `handle_set_config`, an overly large payload claim (`req->value_len >= MAX_VALUE_LEN`) was blindly triggering a potentially large memory copy (`MAX_VALUE_LEN - 1` bytes) from an out-of-bounds user space pointer, which has now been updated to safely reject oversize lengths.

I verified the fixes using `test.sh`, which now passes all validation and fuzz tests securely.
